ScoreSlot.description: One 0.001-wide slice of the band, and what the judge said inside it.

bin_low.description: The slot's lower edge. A pair scoring exactly this lands in this slot; a pair scoring the upper edge lands in the next one.
bin_low.title: Bin Low

different_count.description: Agreed NO readings. This is the count step 1 walks down and the only one that moves the line.
different_count.title: Different Count

same_count.description: Agreed YES readings in this slot.
same_count.title: Same Count

unclear_count.description: Agreed UNCLEAR readings. Counted and never fitted on, so a rising share here is visible rather than silent.
unclear_count.title: Unclear Count

ScoreSlot.title: ScoreSlot

changelog.change: Added judged_dates. An older record reads its counted dates as its memory.
changelog.why: A reset archives the counts, and which nights were read is not a count.

changelog.change: `folded_dates` is now `counted_dates`. The old key still reads.
changelog.why: Borrowed vocabulary for the count this field already holds.

changelog.change: Added judge_temperature, decode_digest and judge_thinks, and stamped them.
changelog.why: Two samplers and two decode envelopes were counted as one population.

changelog.change: Initial shape: a fixed row of slots, three counts each, and the dates counted.
changelog.why: A fit that sorted every pair ever judged would cost more every day.

description: The band, slot by slot, and the dates already counted into it.

band_high.description: The top of the band. 1.00 is the highest a cosine goes, so the top slot is never short of room.
band_high.title: Band High

band_low.description: The lowest score the record holds a slot for. Below it nothing was ever judged, so the record can say nothing about it.
band_low.title: Band Low

bin_width.description: How wide each slot is. This is the resolution of the fitted line: the fit can only ever answer to the nearest slot edge.
bin_width.title: Bin Width

cosine_weight.description: What the cosine was worth for every count in this record. A different weight puts the same pair in a different slot, so a change archives the record rather than reinterpreting it.
cosine_weight.title: Cosine Weight

counted_dates.description: Every date already counted, sorted. A date already here is refused a second time rather than doubling its counts, which makes a re-run free instead of damaging.
counted_dates.title: Counted Dates

decode_digest.description: sha256 of what the judging call asked the decoder to do, minus the prompt, the grammar and the model name - each of which is stamped here in a column of its own. It catches a sampler field that moved with no other column moving, which is a change to what a verdict means that the six named values cannot see.
decode_digest.title: Decode Digest

grammar_digest.description: sha256 of the grammar the verdicts were produced under.
grammar_digest.title: Grammar Digest

judge_model.description: Which model produced these verdicts. Null until the first day is counted.
judge_model.title: Judge Model

judge_temperature.description: The sampler temperature every verdict in this record was decoded at. Null on a record written before the column existed, which is the one value it means: a sampler nobody recorded, not a sampler set to nothing.
judge_temperature.title: Judge Temperature

judge_thinks.description: Whether a reasoning span ran in front of every verdict counted here. A column of its own because `decode_digest` cannot see it: the only posted key a thinking envelope moves is the prompt, and the prompt is excluded. Without it a record counted cold and a record counted after reasoning are one population.
judge_thinks.title: Judge Thinks

judged_dates.description: Every date this judge has ever counted, sorted, and kept when an instrument move archives the counts. The counts are thrown away because they answer a different question afterwards; the fact that a night was read is not a count, so it stays. This is the list the outstanding-nights answer is taken from, and it holds every date in `counted_dates`.
judged_dates.title: Judged Dates

key_point_weight.description: What the key-point term was worth. Same reason as the cosine weight.
key_point_weight.title: Key Point Weight

prompt_digest.description: sha256 of the system turn the verdicts were produced under.
prompt_digest.title: Prompt Digest

scorer_model.description: Which encoder produced the scores these counts were filed under. Null until the first day is counted.
scorer_model.title: Scorer Model

slots.description: The band, slot by slot, lowest first. Fixed size: the record never grows as the archive does, which is why the fit reads it and never the day tree (Guardrail #12).
slots.title: Slots
